summary:
The person began with 0.95 minutes of walking, followed by 0.6 minutes of standing, and 0.12 minutes of sitting. They spent 0.17 minutes in a sitting posture, with a total of three instances of sitting or crouching. The majority of their time was spent walking (66.6 meters), with brief periods of standing and crouching. They moved a chair, walked to a table, and accessed a vending machine, with a significant portion of their time spent on a wooden deck.

To improve posture and schedule, the person should: 1) increase movement during breaks to reduce sitting time, especially during the 0.17-minute sitting period; 2) incorporate 10–15 minutes of stretching or light activity every hour to counteract prolonged sitting; 3) limit standing time to 10–15 minutes per hour and use a standing desk or take short standing breaks to improve posture. These adjustments would help reduce strain and support long-term health.
